audit_findings.title: Current share count and debt are paired with stale interest expense
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt increased $2,012.7m from $9,355.9m at 2025-12-31 to $11,368.6m at 2026-06-30; first-half net interest increased $68.7m year over year; $2,724.1m funded 7.865m share repurchases
audit_findings.mechanism: The share denominator reflects post-2025 repurchases, while anchor OE excludes the associated incremental interest expense; debt-funded repurchases therefore improve per-share value without the matching financing cost.
audit_findings.evidence: Total debt excluding unamortized debt issuance costs was $9,355.9 at December 31, 2025 (32.0% of total capital) as compared to $7,669.2 at December 31, 2024 (28.9% of total capital).
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated, and the filings show that 2026 borrowing principally accompanied repurchases rather than material acquisitions. The precise sustainable after-tax interest adjustment remains unresolved, but the amounts are readily capable of moving the $408.17 base value below the $407.28 market price.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE, debt, cash and fully diluted shares at one date, incorporating post-2025 after-tax interest and any acquired OE; rerun all scenarios with that synchronized claim.

audit_findings.title: Indicor may be added gross of a tax claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $241.5m filed outside-basis deferred tax liability at 2025-12-31; planned instrumentation proceeds are approximately $1,300m pretax versus $1,100m after tax, implying approximately $200m of tax
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds the $1,792.2m Indicor fair-value asset but does not separately deduct taxes payable upon realization.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has a deferred tax liability of $ 241.5 in outside basis difference as of December 31, 2025 associated with the retained minority equity interest in Indicor.
audit_findings.explanation: The $1,792.2m bridge amount equals the latest reported balance-sheet fair value, while the filing expressly distinguishes pretax from after-tax realization proceeds. This demonstrates at least an approximately $200m tax claim on the planned instrumentation proceeds; tax attributable to the remaining flow-controls interest is unresolved. Even $200m equals about $1.96 per valuation share, exceeding the $0.89 base-value premium to market price.
audit_findings.action: Replace the gross bridge asset with transaction-specific after-tax proceeds plus an after-tax value for the remaining Indicor interest, reconciling the outside-basis deferred tax liability and any transaction taxes; rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Historical growth may require acquisition spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $8,960m of acquisition spending over three years, equal to approximately 397% of $2,258.4m anchor OE and 21.5% of $41,706m base equity value; required recurring acquisition charge unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth derived from acquired earnings enters the forecast growth rate, while the acquisition cash needed to obtain that growth is omitted from distributable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In the last three years, we have deployed approximately $8,960 of capital toward acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition dependence and spending scale are demonstrated, but the record does not establish how much of the 7%–9% forecast requires future acquisitions. Reported organic revenue growth of 5.4% in 2025 and 5.3% in first-half 2026 does not by itself validate the higher OE-growth assumptions. Given the acquisition spending relative to OE and equity value, continued acquisition dependence could materially reduce value.
audit_findings.action: Decompose historical OE growth into organic, acquired and financing components; then rerun using either supportable organic OE growth or a recurring acquisition-capital charge sufficient to produce the assumed growth.

audit_findings.title: Null perimeter ignores partial-year contributions from completed acquisitions
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 acquisitions contributed 6.7 percentage points of 2025 revenue growth and 4.1 percentage points of first-half 2026 revenue growth; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A non-annualized 2025 OE anchor can omit earnings from months before acquisition, while an undifferentiated forecast-growth rate may partly count that annualization as recurring organic growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The results of operations of the acquired businesses are included in Roper’s Consolidated Financial Statements from the date of each acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: Partial-year inclusion is demonstrated, but the filings do not disclose acquisition-level OE needed to annualize the anchor. Omitting annualization can understate value; treating annualization as repeatable growth can overstate it. The record therefore cannot establish the net material effect.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a full-year pro forma 2025 OE perimeter for CentralReach, Subsplash and the bolt-ons, including after-tax interest, maintenance investment and integration costs; separate 2026 annualization from organic growth and rerun.

audit_findings.title: Acquired-intangible amortization may be treated as entirely costless
audit_findings.magnitude: $815.4m of 2025 acquired-intangible amortization, equal to 36.1% of $2,258.4m anchor OE; economic replacement cost unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back acquired-intangible amortization increases anchor OE unless recurring customer-retention and technology-replacement expenditures remain deducted elsewhere.
audit_findings.evidence: Amortization expense of other intangible assets was $ 815.4 , $ 745.2 , and $ 698.4 during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The large amortization amount is demonstrated, but an economic error is not yet demonstrated because filed 2025 expenses already include $852.5m of R&D, while $57.3m of capitalized software and $47.4m of capital expenditures may also capture replacement investment. Nevertheless, only a small recurring cost hidden by the $815.4m add-back would erase the base case's $0.89-per-share premium to market, making the unresolved exposure material.
audit_findings.action: Trace every OE adjustment to verify the amortization add-back, map expensed R&D, selling and retention costs, capitalized software and maintenance capex to customer and technology replacement, and rerun with any uncovered recurring replacement cost.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains a favorable tax item that may not recur
audit_findings.magnitude: $25.8m 2025 legal-entity-restructuring tax benefit; if fully included in anchor OE, approximately $451.8m or $4.42 per share of base value using the filed DCF sensitivity
audit_findings.mechanism: A non-recurring tax benefit raises anchor OE and is capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our 2025 effective income tax rate of 20.6% decreased as compared to our 2024 tax rate of 21.2%, due primarily to favorable rate impacts from the recognition of a net tax benefit associated with legal entity restructuring and a reduction in state taxes, partially offset by the non-recurrence of prior year valuation allowance releases.
audit_findings.explanation: The $25.8m benefit is filed and non-operating in character, but whether the OE construction already normalized it must be traced. If fully included, removing it would reduce the indicated base value from $408.17 to approximately $403.75 per share, changing the comparison with the $407.28 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $25.8m tax benefit to the OE calculation, normalize the anchor to the sustainable 21%–22% tax rate where applicable, and rerun all scenarios.
